title: Adaptive Span Fragmentation & Prefill Harmonizer for reduced padding
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce an Adaptive Span Fragmentation (ASF) layer in the micro-batcher that: 1) fragments incoming requests into coherent span groups based on prefix/shared tokens and attention locality hints; 2) coalesces fragments into length-homogeneous micro-batches for kernel affinity; and 3) schedules prefill vs decode paths to minimize padding while preserving p95/p99 latency SLOs. This is intended to reduce padding waste and improve throughput for mixed-length multimodal workloads without breaking existing rollback/fallback behavior.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integration with existing coalescer: ASF must accept the same request API and be toggleable via runtime flag.
Padding token reduction >= 20% on mixed-length production traffic sample (week of 2025-10-20).
No regression in p95 latency (<= +5% from baseline) and p99 increase limited to <= +12% on tail-sensitive routes.
Automated integration tests for kernel-affinity hints and attention-window stitching added to CI.
Canary rollout plan documented and an automatic fallback to legacy coalescer in case of SLA regressions.
implementation_notes: Design ASF as a light-weight pre-processor between request ingress and existing coalescer so we can toggle without schema changes.
Compute fragmentation keys using a rolling bloom on prefix hash + attention-window fingerprint to group requests that will benefit from shared KV cache prefill.
Expose kernel-affinity hint metadata so the scheduler can choose kernel/quantization path (e.g., fp16-gemv vs int8-matmul) per micro-batch.
Schedule prefill-heavy fragments earlier in a cycle, and prioritize pairing long prefill fragments with short decode-only fragments to fill slots and reduce slack.
Add telemetry hooks: pad_tokens_saved, microbatch_shape_histogram, kernel_hint_distribution, per-route tail-latency deltas.
Keep implementation in feature branch runtime/ASF-prefill and target small PRs: core logic, telemetry, scheduler integration, tests, canary toggle.
experiment_results: Synthetic mixed-length benchmark (docs+chat+search mix) on a 4xA100 node pool: pad token reduction = 27% (CI 23-31%).
Cost-per-token proxy (compute secs * GPU price) decreased by ~18% for the benchmark workload after ASF enabled with kernel-affinity hints.
p95 latency delta: +2.8% (within target), p99 delta: +9.6% (observed on long-tail chat route).
Micro-batch utilization improved: mean occupied_activations per batch increased from 62% -> 78%.
Worst-case tail regressions correlated with batching of heterogeneous attention-window fragments — mitigated by tightening fragmentation thresholds.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): Implement feature-flagged ASF in runtime branch and add integration tests (done).
Phase 1 (lab): Run synthetic workloads and kernel selection experiments on canary node pool (complete).
Phase 2 (canary-prod): Enable ASF for 3% of production requests for non-critical routes for 72h with dashboard monitors and auto-rollback thresholds (p95 > baseline +8% OR p99 > baseline +15%).
Phase 3 (gradual): Ramp to 25% over 2 weeks observing pad_tokens_saved and cost metrics, keep fallback policy active.
Phase 4 (full): Promote to default for supported models and expose tuning knobs in Optimize recommendations; document for Dedicated/Private customers.
risks_mitigation: Risk: tail latency regressions on routes with strict p99 requirements. Mitigation: strict canary thresholds and per-route opt-out config; fallback to legacy coalescer on breach.

Risk: kernel affinity hints misaligned with actual model kernel performance (regression on some quantization paths). Mitigation: A/B kernel selection experiments and conservative default affinity mapping; add offline perf calibration job.
Risk: increased scheduler complexity causing resource fragmentation. Mitigation: limit fragmentation depth and introduce a heuristic GC of tiny fragments after X ms.
Risk: telemetry signal noise. Mitigation: instrument padded-token baseline per route and compute rolling windows for alerts, not single-minute spikes.
